summary: The note examines how aging utility infrastructure in the US causes outages and disruptions, citing blackouts and water main breaks in late 2023. It then surveys solutions: smart grids, AI-driven predictive maintenance, public-private partnerships, and community initiatives. It concludes that adaptability, sustainable investment, and collaboration are key to more reliable utilities.
one_line: Overview of how aging US utility infrastructure drives outages and of smart grid, predictive maintenance, partnership, and community solutions.
key_facts: On October 23, 2023, more than 100,000 residents in Harrisonburg, Virginia, woke up to a complete blackout.

A National Utility Service Reliability Council (NUSRC) study released September 3, 2023, found 65% of the nation's electrical grid components are over 25 years old, with transmission lines past the half-century mark.

On October 12, 2023, a water main break in Plano, Texas, disrupted services to over 250,000 residents; the main dated to the 1970s and its replacement had been deferred multiple times due to budget constraints.
Dr. Emily Nguyen of the Advanced Utility Systems Institute said at a September 15, 2023, conference that much infrastructure has outlived its intended lifespan.
Internet providers struggle with coaxial cables installed in the 1990s that were not designed for today's high-speed data demands.
Boulder, Colorado began implementing a smart electric grid in early 2024, expected to cut outage frequency and duration through self-healing fault isolation.

Charlotte, North Carolina's water utility started a predictive maintenance program on August 18, 2023, using acoustic sensors and machine learning to find and fix weaknesses in its distribution network.

Davenport Electric Company in Iowa began a wholesale redesign of its electrical distribution network on December 3, 2023, adding weather-resistant alloy power lines and auto-reclosing circuit breakers.
On September 12, 2023, Knoxville, Tennessee partnered with GreenTech Renewables to replace and reinforce the city's gas, water, and electrical grids, backed by federal grants and private investment.
Sunnyside Neighborhood Association in Portland, Oregon launched a crowd-funding campaign on November 15, 2023, to convert street lights to LEDs.
The University of Michigan began offering public workshops on infrastructure literacy as of September 8, 2023.
John Carter, CEO of NextGen Utility Solutions, said on November 1, 2023, that the industry is on the cusp of a 'renaissance in utility service provision.'
